llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the xlsx file and extracts column C (Old ID) and D (New 7 Digit ID) for rows 2-31, plus cell E1 — matching exactly the two instruction requirements.
Zero-padding check (r.get('d') == str(r['c']).zfill(7)) is semantically correct: TEXT() formula stores strings in xlsx, so openpyxl returns strings and the comparison works.
E1 check (int(e1) == max_expected) with expected.get('max_expected', 21540) uses correct direct-access pattern for type='rule' — no erroneous .get('rules') wrapper.
Both instruction sub-goals are verified with partial credit (0.5 each); coverage is complete.
Postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation; data_only=True reads cached formula results — state freshness is handled.
Expected value max_expected=21540 is confirmed by trajectory summary and scoring_breakdown.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: The rule_validation_passed=false in this section reflects old pre-fix hash issues; actual function files already use the correct 32-char hash — no functional fix needed.
Minor: getter reads up to row 31 but the trajectory filled D2:D30 (29 rows); rows beyond the data range return c_val=None and are skipped correctly — no issue in practice.
